# Extra analysis (generated by analysis_extras.py)

## 1. Uncertainty on the headline numbers (test set: 96 spam, 678 ham)

| quantity | count | rate | 95% interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| NB (thr 0.5) false-positive rate | 5/678 | 0.0074 | [0.0032, 0.0171] |
| NB (thr 0.5) spam recall | 85/96 | 0.8854 | [0.8064, 0.9348] |
| LogReg tuned false-positive rate | 1/678 | 0.0015 | [0.0003, 0.0083] |
| LogReg tuned spam recall | 90/96 | 0.9375 | [0.8703, 0.9710] |

The NB and LogReg intervals overlap on both quantities, so the test set cannot prove one model is better. One extra false positive moves the FPR by about 0.15 points.

## 2. Naive Bayes probabilities are extreme

On the test set, 92.8% of messages get P(spam) below 0.01 or above 0.99; only 3.0% fall between 0.1 and 0.9. A threshold has little room to trade precision for recall, and tuning it is unstable.

## 3. Did the dev-tuned NB threshold transfer to test?

Threshold chosen on dev for FPR <= 0.5%: 0.3132.

| split | ham FPR | spam recall |
|---|---|---|
| dev | 0.0044 | 0.938 |
| test | 0.0103 | 0.885 |

The target was met on dev but exceeded on test, so the tuned threshold did not generalise.
